cognition_model.summary: A high-altitude herd citizen with a guard's streak: it hums its moods, keeps its herd's social order, remembers Andean routes, and — uniquely in this batch — earns a living protecting other species, confronting predators it has been bonded to oppose.

personality.mbti_label: Lore-based interpretive read (fan interpretation) — a behaviour-design lens, not a measurement. Basis here: documented behaviour.
personality.justification: A vigilant herd-guardian and companion: it keeps watch over its group — even an adopted flock of sheep — hums its feelings to everyone nearby, remembers its people and pastures, and charges trouble on the herd's behalf.

skills: Livestock guarding (documented use against canid predators)
behavior_model: Triggers: canid silhouette near the flock -> alarm call and charge (guard-bonded individuals); stranger approach -> stare, ear signals, spit as last resort; pasture rotation -> herd procession. Needs: herd company, high pasture, dung-pile sites. Goals: herd safety and standing. State changes: graze-scan-guard rotation shared with herd-mates.
relationships: Camelidae; the dromedary's kin in this batch — one family domesticated on two continents for the same virtues. Socially a herd animal; guard llamas bond to their charges across species, a relationship this record treats as real social behaviour.
memory_model: Remembers: herd-mates, charges, routes, pastures and handlers. Forgets: little of social consequence. Misreads: dogs near the flock are read as coyotes until proven otherwise — the guard's standing bias.
confidence_and_conflicts: INFERRED: no brain figure stated per the brief's list. Guard-llama effectiveness is documented in agricultural studies/surveys; cognition claims otherwise stay at social/spatial level. Spitting is described accurately as a last-resort, mostly intra-herd signal — not the cartoon version.
